title: Aurum Software - Procurement MSA/DPA/SLA Review
summary: Redwood AE/SE reviewed standard MSA and DPA language, SLA tiers and pricing approval path. Customer legal flagged logging and data residency requirements; procurement asked about onboarding timeline and PO process. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share redline-friendly MSA/DPA PDFs, pricing worksheet, and schedule onboarding kickoff next week.
next_steps: Nora to send editable MSA + DPA and pricing worksheet by 2026-06-27
Priya to share expected ingestion volumes and PII flow diagram by 2026-06-29
Ethan to confirm PO process and approved vendor list by 2026-07-02
action_items: Nora: attach MSA (word) and DPA (word) and pricing worksheet; include change-log - due 2026-06-27
Samir: prepare technical appendix for VPC/private deployment, KMS integration notes - due 2026-06-29
Priya: send ingestion volumes and network diagram - due 2026-06-29

transcript:
Header: 2026-06-25 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~55m
Attendees: Nora Patel (Redwood AE), Samir Zhao (Redwood SE), Maya Rodriguez (Aurum Legal), Ethan Cole (Aurum Procurement), Priya Nair (Aurum Eng)

[00:00] Nora: Hey everyone, thanks for joining; quick agenda — MSA/DPA review, SLA questions, pricing and onboarding. Sound good?
[00:12] Maya: Yep, thanks. We just want to make sure data residency and logging are handled, and our legal team will likely redline the standard DPA.
[00:20] Samir: Totally expected. We have an editable DPA that we can send; it includes KMS integration and customer-managed key options for private deployments.
[00:30] Ethan: Good. From procurement side we need estimated spend and an expected start date for PO'ing the contract. Also any vendor forms for security questionnaires.
[00:42] Nora: We'll share the pricing worksheet — it has hosted vs dedicated vs private TCO examples. For onboarding timeline, typical procurement to kickoff is 2–3 weeks once MSA + PO are signed.
[01:05] Priya: On the engineering side we want clarity on SLA uptime and credits, plus what metrics are included in the SLA. Also curious about KV cache persistence for private mode — how logs and KV are retained.
[01:18] Samir: SLA is 99.9% for dedicated; hosted has tiered SLOs. Credits are pro-rated and there is an incident dispute process. KV cache is ephemeral for hosted but configurable for private/dedicated; logs retention is configurable and we can support shorter retention periods for PII.
[01:38] Maya: Are you SOC 2 and ISO certified? Our security team will want evidence.
[01:45] Nora: Yes, SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 reports available under NDA. We'll attach the attestation and the audit contact.
[01:55] Ethan: For DPA, we need stronger language on subprocessor notifications and a 30-day notice on changes.
[02:05] Maya: And we need an explicit clause about data export and deletion timelines post-contract.
[02:12] Samir: Standard is deletion within 30 days after termination for hosted; for Private we can map to customer-controlled retention and KMS deletion. We can add explicit SLA around deletion.
[02:30] Nora: Noted. We'll produce a redline-friendly version. Any constraints on data residency? You mentioned EU earlier?
[02:40] Priya: Aurum has EU customers; we need EU region processing and a clause that data at rest can be kept in region. Also want a list of subprocessors and country-level controls.
[02:52] Samir: We can provide per-region deployments and support VPC peering. Subprocessor list is maintained and we'll provide current as of the contract date.
[03:05] Ethan: On pricing approvals — we run this through a procurement committee. What's the approval cadence for price or discounts?
[03:15] Nora: For committed Dedicated reservations we have a discount ladder based on commit length and GPU types. We'll include a proposed term sheet for procurement to review. If you need a special SOW or addenda, we can support that.
[03:30] Maya: We sometimes need to redline indemnity language; is Redwood open to mutual indemnities or limits on liability?
[03:38] Nora: We'd prefer mutual limited indemnity; we can discuss specific caps. Standard approach is mutual with carve-outs for willful misconduct. We'll flag legal for negotiation.
[03:50] Priya: Technical question — how does Redwood handle encryption keys for Private deployment if we bring our own KMS?
[03:58] Samir: For Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM via standard key wrapping; you keep control. We log access for audit and can surface the logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export.
[04:12] Ethan: Need confirmation on SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; we have to onboard multiple teams.
[04:20] Nora: Support SAML SSO and SCIM; RBAC can be scoped per team and we can map groups. We'll include the SSO guide.
[04:32] Maya: On SLAs, if there's an outage that crosses the SLO, what's the credit calculation?
[04:40] Samir: Credits are percentage-based against monthly invoice depending on downtime bucket; we can share the SLA schedule in the appendix.
[04:50] Ethan: Any red flags re: export controls or restricted data types?
[04:57] Samir: For regulated data we recommend Private deployment and customer-managed KMS. We also support contractual controls in the DPA.
[05:10] Nora: Next steps: we'll send the editable MSA and DPA, pricing worksheet, SOC2 evidence under NDA, and schedule a brief technical onboarding once MSA is agreed.
[05:22] Priya: Can Samir include a short technical appendix describing VPC, private endpoints, KV cache behavior and ingress/egress bandwidth assumptions?
[05:30] Samir: Yep, I'll draft that and send it along with the docs.
[05:36] Maya: Great. Procurement will want to see a final term sheet for Dedicated vs Hosted pricing — include commit levels.
[05:44] Nora: We'll include multiple SKU scenarios and a recommended configuration based on the volumes you share.
[05:52] Ethan: Sounds good. We'll take a look and aim to get redlines back within a week.
[05:58] Nora: Thanks all. We'll follow up by Friday with the package.

End of call.
